R868.note: jwt.verify() with an explicit algorithm allowlist and try/catch correctly closes the trust bypass; requires a new JWT_SECRET env var, a necessary and openly disclosed addition.

R869.note: Sound design (drops the shell, runs ping/nslookup directly with an allowlist) but the rewritten file imports fmt and net, both now unused - verified with go build: 'imported and not used' for each, so it would not compile as written.

R870.note: verifyWith()/parseSignedClaims() are jjwt 0.12.x-only APIs; the file's pom.xml pins jjwt 0.11.5, which only exposes setSigningKey()/parseClaimsJws(), so this would not compile against the stated dependency without also bumping it (not mentioned); it also omits the try/catch needed to turn a verification failure into the 401 the explanation itself says is required.

R871.note: Good design (argument array plus an allowlist that also rejects a leading '-' for flag injection) but the rewritten file still imports "fmt", now unused - verified with go build: 'imported and not used'; would not compile.

R872.note: The arithmetic-only regex gate runs before either the bc subprocess or the ExpressionLanguage evaluator, so no shell/code injection can reach either path; preserves the ok/result contract.

R873.note: Exact == comparison matches the stated contract precisely: true only on exact match, false for empty/partial otherwise.

R874.note: GetFullPath + GetRelativePath with '..'/rooted checks correctly contains the path against traversal and absolute-path bypass on both separator styles; legitimate filenames pass through unchanged.

R875.note: self.get_object() restores DRF's queryset-scoped lookup and object-permission check; since get_queryset() already filters to the owner's rows, another user's invoice 404s exactly as the contract requires (indistinguishable from missing).

R876.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes() is the correct CSPRNG replacement; output is still Base64-encoded and returned the same way as before.

R877.note: Parameterized SLF4J call with a control-character-escaping encoder closes CRLF log forging; the trailing Throwable is still attached and both branches/status codes are unchanged.

R878.note: CGI::escapeHTML on both interpolated values neutralizes the injection while leaving the rest of the markup unchanged.

R879.note: magic.from_buffer()'s detected-and-allowlisted type is used for ContentType, never the caller value, matching the contract; but it also drops the key/content_type parameters in favor of a generated uuid key, an unrelated signature change (any existing caller passing key would break) not flagged as a required follow-up.

R880.note: Clearing session.Values before writing the authenticated identity is the correct mitigation given gorilla/sessions CookieStore has no separate ID to regenerate (store.Get and store.New both decode the incoming cookie identically); no other behavior changed.

R881.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection and gates the route with csrfProtection, but no route anywhere calls reply.generateCsrf() to hand a token to the client, so a legitimate browser has no way to ever obtain a valid token - every POST, forged or legitimate, would now fail CSRF validation; this breakage is not disclosed.

R882.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param/execute correctly parameterizes the query; mysqli_stmt_get_result preserves the same result/null contract as the original mysqli_query call.

R883.note: execSync(command, options) does not accept an argument array as its second parameter - verified in Node: execSync('echo', ['hello','world']) silently ignores the array and just runs 'echo' with no args. As written, sourcePath/geometry/thumbPath are never passed to convert, so no thumbnail is ever produced; the write-up's claim that it 'maintains the same behavior' is false, and this is not disclosed. execFileSync/spawnSync is the API that actually supports this shape.

R884.note: Only allowlists the caller-supplied content_type string and still stores that same caller value as ContentType; never inspects file_bytes, so the contract's 'reject on actual-bytes mismatch / never the caller-supplied value' requirement is not met, leaving a content-sniffing mismatch open (e.g. HTML bytes labeled image/png).

R885.note: exec.CommandContext binds archiveName as the single argument to -f (not an independent positional token), removing the shell and closing the injection without enabling multi-flag tar option injection; success/failure behavior is unchanged.

R886.note: encode_entities() on both interpolated fields neutralizes the injection without altering the rest of the markup.

R887.note: Adds the missing receivedByteCount >= 2+length check before the memmove, exactly closing the OOB read while leaving the existing capacity check and return contract untouched.
